TCP_Flood.ocpp_impact: Overwhelms the Charge Point or CSMS network interface. Prevents legitimate OCPP WebSocket heartbeats and transaction messages from being processed.

UDP_Flood.ocpp_impact: Consumes bandwidth and router processing power. May drop the OCPP WebSocket connection leading to temporary 'Denial of Charge'.

SYN_Flood.ocpp_impact: Exhausts TCP connection limits on the charger or backend, preventing new EV drivers from initiating charging sessions (Authorize/StartTransaction).

PSHACK_Flood.ocpp_impact: Forces the system to process empty or garbage data, wasting CPU cycles on the CSMS or Charge Point.

TCP_Port_Scan.ocpp_impact: Reconnaissance. Attacker is looking for open ports (e.g., SSH, HTTP, WebSocket) on the charging station to find unpatched firmware vulnerabilities.

SYN_Stealth_Scan.ocpp_impact: Covert reconnaissance to map the EV charging network topology without completing TCP handshakes and avoiding basic firewall logs.

Vulnerability_Scan.ocpp_impact: Active probing for known CVEs in the charger's web interface or outdated firmware.

Service_Version_Detection.ocpp_impact: Attacker is attempting to identify the exact OS and OCPP server version to craft a targeted exploit.

OS_Fingerprinting.ocpp_impact: Identifying the underlying operating system (e.g., embedded Linux) of the Charge Point.

Aggressive_Scan.ocpp_impact: Loud, high-speed probing for vulnerabilities across all services. Often precedes a direct exploit attempt.

Slowloris_Scan.ocpp_impact: Ties up HTTP/WebSocket connections by sending partial requests slowly. Can completely freeze the charger's communication module.

SynonymousIP_Flood.ocpp_impact: Spoofed IP flooding designed to bypass basic IP filtering and crash the endpoint.
